pending_commit.commit_message: chromeos-touch-common.sh: Allow finding fw_link using 2 HW ID(s) Product ID alone is not sufficient to distinguish anymore, as Soraka has 2 different vendors supplying the same panel. So we'd like to allow to use upto 2 ID(s), before falling to the default firmware file. This also helps the case where the default file has to be selected based on one of the IDs. BUG=b:64236305, b:69570672 TEST=verified manually by renaming the firmware files differently that the firmware can find files in all cases. Change-Id: Ifd729aeabac6b2f792cae3b98fe7fcc99ae548d2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/890399 Commit-Ready: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Tested-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

chromeos-wacom-touch-firmware-update.sh: Add detect hardware id Change wacom touch firmware update script flow to detect hardware id first, if there is hardware id exist in the tocuh ic, then select the firmware based on the hardware id, if no then check the product id, if product id is OK, select the firmware based on the product id, otherwise, select the firmware by default. The wacom_flash.query.policy is updated to allow the nanosleep() syscall that is now used by the utility to get hardware id. CQ-DEPEND=CL:753567 BUG=b:64236305 TEST=Verify on Soraka that the firmware are picked up in the following order (the next one if picked if the first one is not available): wacom2_firmware_<hardware_id>.hex wacom2_firmware_<product_id>.hex wacom2_firmware.hex wacom_firmware_<hardware_id>.hex wacom_firmware_<product_id>.hex wacom_firmware.hex Change-Id: I395f02e21ec2416b3af84e24a6fd5d28b54ec088 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/753268 Commit-Ready: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Tested-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

Relax and statically verify QEMU cpu features. Remove pinetrail code which is obsolete. Also do not use qemu64 CPU by default, which has a very limited feature set. Instead request by default to use the Haswell CPU feature set, which is the lowest common denominator on Chrome OS infrastructure. Adding "check" should warn the user when the requested features are not available locally. Furthermore add command line option "kvm_cpu" to allow arbitrary CPU feature set selection. CHROMIUM: config: Add chromiumos-qualcomm config This change adds a chromiumos-qualcomm.flavour.config. It would contain the minimal set of configs needed to boot the SDM845 MTP to RAM disk, except that it was normalized. So the needed configs that are not yet in this tree got obliterated. That was done so that this change could land while still having "normalize config" be a no-op. I'll put a second change on top of this one in a moment that enables the missing features, though that part cannot land until the features they enable do. BUG=chromium:795946 TEST=Build Rajendra's tree and boot cheza to RAM disk. Change-Id: I5de6ee5909b053b7b42578a47262f6cea6d898f4 Signed-off-by: Evan Green <evgreen@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/887920 Commit-Ready: Evan Green <evgreen@google.com> Tested-by: Evan Green <evgreen@google.com> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

Add support for HW alerts - Add a vendor command that provides alert counter. Userspace can use it e.g. for user metric analysis. - Add 'alerts' debug console command. It provides information about chip alerts: supported alerts, fuse status, interrupt status, alert counter. - Add 'alerts fire [INT]' command to fire a software defined alert (globalsec/fwN where N is 0,1,2,3). g: protect flash operations Flash operations in do_flash_op() involve waiting polling for the chip to complete the operation. If a concurrent operation is started while another operation is in progress, flash gets confused and locks up. Let's add a mutex to ensure that flash operation runs to completion before another operation starts. BRANCH=cr50 BUG=b:67651754 TEST=multiple times ran firmware update while the device was coming up and saving TPM status in NVMEM. Observed no failures.
